title: The hybrid readout: frozen ridge + one trained linear residual head on the C4 138k codes
registered_in: analysis/RESEARCH_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_v23.md section 4 M161 / section 6 build entry (17 Aug 2026)
question: Does the unmeasured middle — closed-form ridge + a small trained residual head on the same codes — beat either pure readout?

level.note: the C4 138k context (the M146 level): the first 138,000 rows of the cached full-train codes

sparse.note: the M146 r2 construction for the residual head: HeadOnly (no hidden layer), frozen codes with power_norm

schedule.note: the M109 shared schedule (AdamW, cosine), identical for the pure head and the hybrid

anchors.note: the frozen ridge read (p=0.5, penalty 1.0) is the anchor; the pure trained head is reported against the sealed r2 0.042608695652173914

gate.registered: hybrid >= ridge + 0.005 on the test rows, else archived as a scoped negative (the hybrid must also beat the pure trained head's read to be the best readout).
gate.consequence_passed: the hybrid beats both parents: the ridge's frozen knowledge and the trained residual are complementary.
gate.consequence_fired: the hybrid does not clear the margin: M161 closes as a scoped negative and the pure ridge stays the readout.
